lucky-boar \ud83d\udc17.name: NAFNet-GAN Poisson-Gaussian Microscopy Denoiser
lucky-boar \ud83d\udc17.description: NAFNet-GAN is a supervised denoising model for 2D fluorescence microscopy images affected by realistic Poisson-Gaussian noise. It was developed for the AI4Life Microscopy Supervised Denoising Challenge 2025 and presented at ISBI 2026. The model was trained on the Poisson-Gaussian microscopy dataset, which includes confocal, two-photon, and widefield images from diverse biological samples. It uses a NAFNet-based adversarial framework to reduce noise while preserving fine image structures and the original input intensity range.

resourceful-sheep \ud83d\udc11.name: NAFNet-GAN Tribolium Multiphoton Denoiser
resourceful-sheep \ud83d\udc11.description: NAFNet-GAN is a supervised denoising model for single 2D slices from CARE Tribolium castaneum multiphoton fluorescence microscopy stacks. It was developed for Dataset 2 of the AI4Life Microscopy Supervised Denoising Challenge 2025 and presented at ISBI 2026 in the paper “NAFNet-GAN: An Adversarial Framework for Supervised Fluorescence Microscopy Denoising.” The model uses a NAFNet-based adversarial framework to reduce low-light microscopy noise while preserving biological structures and restoring the original input intensity range.

determined-cricket \ud83e\udd97.name: NAFNet-GAN Planaria Spinning-Disk Denoiser
determined-cricket \ud83e\udd97.description: NAFNet-GAN is a supervised denoising model for single 2D slices from CARE Schmidtea mediterranea fluorescence microscopy stacks acquired with spinning-disk microscopy. It was developed for Dataset 1 of the AI4Life Microscopy Supervised Denoising Challenge 2025 and presented at ISBI 2026 in the paper “NAFNet-GAN: An Adversarial Framework for Supervised Fluorescence Microscopy Denoising.” The model uses a NAFNet-based adversarial framework to reduce low-light microscopy noise while preserving biological structures and restoring the original input intensity range.

diplomatic-orangutan \ud83e\udda7.name: NAFNet-GAN Noisy Nuclei Microscopy Denoiser
diplomatic-orangutan \ud83e\udda7.description: NAFNet-GAN is a supervised denoising model for 2D fluorescence microscopy images of nuclei acquired with widefield and confocal microscopy. It was developed for Dataset 3 of the AI4Life Microscopy Supervised Denoising Challenge 2025 and presented at ISBI 2026 in the paper “NAFNet-GAN: An Adversarial Framework for Supervised Fluorescence Microscopy Denoising.” The model was trained using both small and large nuclei-image crops to reduce severe acquisition noise while preserving nuclear structures and restoring the original input intensity range.

idealistic-eagle \ud83e\udd85.name: Cellpose-SAM
idealistic-eagle \ud83e\udd85.description: Modern algorithms for biological segmentation can match inter-human agreement in annotation quality. This however is not a performance bound: a hypothetical human-consensus segmentation could reduce error rates in half. To obtain a model that generalizes better we adapted the pretrained transformer backbone of a foundation model (SAM) to the Cellpose framework. The resulting Cellpose-SAM model substantially outperforms inter-human agreement and approaches the human-consensus bound. We increase generalization performance further by making the model robust to channel shuffling, cell size, shot noise, downsampling, isotropic and anisotropic blur. The new model can be readily adopted into the Cellpose ecosystem which includes finetuning, human-in-the-loop training, image restoration and 3D segmentation approaches. These properties establish Cellpose-SAM as a foundation model for biological segmentation. This entry ships the cpsam_v2 checkpoint; the architecture is unchanged from cpsam, only the weights differ.

famous-sheep.name: CellposeDINO ViT-L 2D Microscopy Instance Segmenter
famous-sheep.description: CellposeDINO with a DINOv3 ViT-L backbone for instance segmentation of 2D microscopy images. Following Cellpose-SAM v2, the network takes three input channels. Single-channel images should be replicated across all three. The network predicts Cellpose flows and cell probability. BioImage.IO flow dynamics converts them into uint16 labels.

passionate-bug.name: CellposeDINO ViT-B 2D Microscopy Instance Segmenter
passionate-bug.description: CellposeDINO with a DINOv3 ViT-B backbone for instance segmentation of 2D microscopy images. Following Cellpose-SAM v2, the network takes three input channels. Single-channel images should be replicated across all three. The network predicts Cellpose flows and cell probability. BioImage.IO flow dynamics converts them into uint16 labels.

vain-shark \ud83e\udd88.description: This model was trained using Noise2Void (N2V) in CAREamics to denoise 3D images of nuclear mScarlet signal. It was developed as part of AI4Life Open Calls Project 11: 3D Matrix Motility Map (3DM³).

elegant-leopard \ud83d\udc06.name: OC2-23 ResMatching digital expansion microscopy (3D)
elegant-leopard \ud83d\udc06.description: 3D conditional flow matching model (ResMatching) that restores in-vivo two-photon image stacks so that they resemble 4x expansion microscopy. Trained on synthetic low-resolution inputs simulated from expansion microscopy ground truth. Returns the MMSE over 4 samples (10 Euler steps each) and the pixel-wise standard deviation as an uncertainty map.

knowledgeable-mouse.name: CochleaNet SGN Segmentation
knowledgeable-mouse.description: 3D U-Net for the instance segmentation of spiral ganglion neurons (SGNs) in light-sheet microscopy of cleared cochleae, stained for parvalbumin (PV) or calretinin (CR). It predicts the foreground probability, the distance to the object center, and the distance to the object boundary. A seeded watershed turns these maps into SGN instances. Trained on annotated PV-stained mouse cochleae at 0.38 um isotropic voxel size.

content-fish.name: CochleaNet IHC Segmentation
content-fish.description: 3D U-Net for the instance segmentation of inner hair cells (IHCs) in light-sheet microscopy of cleared cochleae, stained for VGlut3 or Myosin VIIa. It predicts the foreground probability, the distance to the object center, and the distance to the object boundary. A seeded watershed turns these maps into IHC instances. Trained on annotated VGlut3-stained mouse and gerbil cochleae at 0.38 um isotropic voxel size.

loyal-ant.name: CochleaNet Ribbon Synapse Detection
loyal-ant.description: 3D U-Net for the detection of ribbon synapses in light-sheet microscopy of cleared cochleae, stained for CtBP2. It predicts a heatmap with a Gaussian peak at each synapse. Local maxima of the heatmap give the synapse positions. Trained on annotated CtBP2-stained cochleae at 0.38 um isotropic voxel size.

nervous-shark.name: CochleaNet Low-Resolution SGN Segmentation
nervous-shark.description: Anisotropic 3D U-Net for the instance segmentation of spiral ganglion neurons (SGNs) in lower-resolution light-sheet microscopy of cleared cochleae, stained for parvalbumin (PV). It predicts the foreground probability, the distance to the object center, and the distance to the object boundary. A seeded watershed turns these maps into SGN instances. Trained on annotated PV-stained mouse and marmoset cochleae from a LaVision UltraMicroscope at 1.887779 x 1.887779 x 3.0 um voxel size (x, y, z).

confused-cow.name: CochleaNet Low-Resolution IHC Segmentation
confused-cow.description: 3D U-Net for the instance segmentation of inner hair cells (IHCs) in lower-resolution light-sheet microscopy of cleared cochleae, stained for Myosin VIIa, calretinin (CR) or VGlut3. It predicts the foreground probability, the distance to the object center, and the distance to the object boundary. A seeded watershed turns these maps into IHC instances. Trained on annotated mouse and marmoset cochleae at about 1.89 x 1.89 x 3.0 um voxel size (x, y, z).

nice-flamingo \ud83e\udda9.name: Cellpose-DINO ViT-B (cpdino-vitb) grayscale
nice-flamingo \ud83e\udda9.description:
Cellpose-DINO ViT-B (cpdino-vitb weights), the generalist cell and nucleus segmentation model of Cellpose 4 (DINOv3's ViT-B/16 encoder with 8-pixel token stride), for single-channel (grayscale) 2D images. Re-implemented with BiaPy, so it does not need the cellpose package. It outputs Cellpose's raw maps, named with BiaPy's channel codes: 'F' (cell probability, after a sigmoid), 'Gv' and 'Gh' (vertical and horizontal flows, x5). Cellpose's flow-following post-processing turns them into instances (as BiaPy does when consuming it).
representation: F+Gv+Gh
